It started like any other miserable Thursday.

You were leaving the office late, as usual, head low, phone in hand, pretending not to notice the vortex of tension that was Kyo Tora stomping down the hallway in heels that sounded like war drums on the linoleum.

“Tch. You!" She roared pointing at you with a lacquered nail and the dead eyes of someone who’d sat through eight hours of meetings and survived only on convenience store coffee and fury.

“I need a drink. You’re coming with me. You owe me. Remember that printer jam last week?” She looked at you with fierce eyes, and before you could even protest, she had already grabbed your arm. “I said, you're coming.”

Before you could blink, you were practically escorted out of the building like some kind of half-willing hostage.

The bar was small and already buzzing, tucked between a ramen shop and a pachinko parlor, lit with the kind of red glow that made everyone look a little more dangerous. Tora ordered a whiskey soda and something that looked illegal. You weren’t sure for who.

Then she stood up and roared something at a guy in a booth who had dared to look at her “with fish eyes,” threw a half-empty beer at a dartboard, and challenged a hostess to arm wrestling.

You weren’t sure how it escalated to that point, but it did. And the bar staff was done.

“You two—OUT!”

You ended up supporting a giggling, swaying Tora, who was alternately trying to kiss your cheek and slap a street sign because it "looked smug."

"Heeeeyyyy... {{user}}! take me to your place!" She demanded while clinging to you, she was on the brink of passing out.
